D005-D018_h001.question: It's been a tough couple of months, doctor. The restaurant usually keeps me so busy, but lately, it feels like I'm barely holding it together. I keep feeling these crawling sensations on my skin, like bugs, even when there's nothing there. It started about two months ago, and it's Constant. And then there are these thoughts... I know it sounds strange, but I truly believe I have a unique insight into the future of the culinary world, a gift, really, that no one else possesses. It’s hard to explain, but it feels incredibly real. My husband notices I'm not myself; he says I'm distant. Everything just feels... different. It's like I'm hyper-aware of everything around me, but also disconnected at the same time.
D005-D018_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D018_h001.answer: D & C. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h002.question:
"Lately, things have been… off. It's tough to explain, but I feel like people are talking about me, even when they're just on the bus or something. Like, I’ll hear a snippet of conversation, and suddenly, I know it’s about me. Even the news, sometimes it feels like the anchorman is giving me direct messages. And the things I see… for about two months now, I’ve been catching glimpses of people or shadows that aren’t really there, especially out of the corner of my eye. It’s like, a flicker, then they’re gone. It makes wiring pretty difficult sometimes.

I guess this all really kicked off after... that accident at the worksite. There was a big explosion, and I was pretty shaken up. Since then, it’s just been harder to focus, and I keep feeling this dread, like something bad is always about to happen. I haven’t been able to sleep well since then either, and I have these awful nightmares. But it’s these visions and the feeling that I'm being targeted that really get to me. It's making it hard to trust anyone, or even just walk down the street."
D005-D018_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D018_h002.answer: D & C. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h003.question: "It's been a rough couple of months, maybe two now. I just feel... off. My boyfriend, Mark, he’s been acting really distant, and I *know* he's seeing someone else from the store. He denies it, but I see the way he looks at the new girl, Sarah. Little things, you know? A late text, a cancelled plan... It all adds up. And then there are the voices. Sometimes I hear whispers when I'm alone in my apartment, or even at work when things are quiet, like someone's calling my name, or talking about me. It's usually indistinct, but sometimes I hear Mark's voice, accusing me, or Sarah's, laughing. It's not constant, which is why I haven't really said anything until now. It just makes it hard to focus, to manage the girls at the store, to even sleep sometimes."
D005-D018_h003.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D018_h003.answer: D & C. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h004.question: It's been about two months now, and things just feel…off. Not in a good way, more like a coded message I can’t quite decipher, but I know it's there. And the smells… I keep smelling burnt rubber, sometimes something acrid and metallic, even when no one else does. It’s disorienting, especially when I’m trying to focus. My wife, she’s noticed I’m not myself. Things are just… tense.

Sometimes, I also feel this crawly sensation, like bugs or something under my skin. It’s not always there, but it’s enough to make me uncomfortable. My wife, she says I’m imagining things, but it feels so real. Honestly, I'm just looking for some answers, some relief.

D005-D018_h006.question: It’s been a rough seven months, doctor. Ever since my husband passed, things just… aren’t right. I try to keep up with my housekeeping, but it’s hard when I feel like I’m constantly being watched. I know it sounds silly, but I have this persistent feeling that the neighbors, or maybe even those people from the utility company, are somehow monitoring me. I catch myself doing these odd little gestures, like adjusting my apron just so, or clearing my throat in a particular way – almost as if I need to perform correctly. Nothing brings me joy anymore. The flowers in the garden, the ones my husband loved, just don’t bring a smile to my face. Even looking at old photos of us feels… flat. I just miss him, and everything feels so strange now.
D005-D018_h006.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D018_h006.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h007.question: It’s been almost seven months now, and honestly, I just feel… different. I sometimes feel like I have this incredible, almost magical connection to my students, like I can instinctively know what they need, even before they do. It’s a powerful feeling, like I’m meant for something really special, beyond just teaching. But then, there are these other times. I find myself just… rocking. Back and forth, back and forth, almost without realizing it, especially when I’m alone in my apartment. And lately, talking feels like a chore. The words just aren't there, or they come out so slowly. My boss has noticed, she keeps asking if everything’s alright, but I just can't explain it. It’s all just so… quiet, inside and out. It’s not like anything I’ve ever felt before.
D005-D018_h007.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D018_h007.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h008.question: It's been about seven months now. I just don't find joy in things like I used to. The weekly volunteer work at the shelter, which used to be my solace after Arthur passed, feels…flat. I go through the motions, but the sparkle is gone. And these thoughts, doctor, they've become quite persistent. I’ve started to believe I have a special gift, a connection to something larger, almost as if I can influence events with my thoughts. It's a heavy responsibility, this power. Sometimes, I find myself just rocking back and forth, or tapping my fingers for long stretches without even realizing it until someone asks if I’m alright. It's not like me at all. There was a terrible accident last year, a car crash, that left me feeling quite shaken, but these other…feelings, they feel different, somehow.
D005-D018_h008.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D018_h008.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h009.question:
"Lately, things have been… off. It’s hard to explain, but I feel like I’ve got this incredible knack for understanding electrical currents that nobody else does. Like, I can see the energy flowing, almost predict how it's going to arc before it even happens. It’s more than just being good at my job; it’s like a gift, a special insight.

Sometimes, though, it’s like my brain just shuts down. I’ll be working, or even just trying to talk to someone, and my mind goes blank. The words just won’t come out, and I clam up. It’s not that I don’t know what to say, it’s just… gone. And there are times, whole stretches, where I can barely move, just standing there, staring, not really seeing anything. The guys at work ask if I’m okay, but I can’t really answer. It’s been like this for about seven months now.

There are also these moments, quick flashes really, of that accident. The explosion, the heat… it’s like I’m right back there, even though I know I’m not. I don’t really dwell on it, but it just pops up sometimes, out of nowhere."
D005-D018_h009.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D018_h009.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h010.question: It’s been about seven months now that things have felt… off. Everything feels like it's heading for a complete collapse, like the whole planet is just going to unravel. Sometimes, I’ll be talking to someone, and my mind just blanks. The words are there, but they don't come out right, or maybe I just don't feel like saying them. And then other times, I just get this overwhelming urge to giggle at the most inappropriate moments, like when I'm supposed to be serious, and I can't stop myself. It's not like me. I used to be able to talk for ages, tell stories, but now… it's just harder to string thoughts together. It’s not constant, these feelings, but they’re there, lurking.
D005-D018_h010.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia

    D. Delusional Disorder
D005-D018_h010.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h011.question:
It’s been a really tough few months, probably about four now. Things just feel… off. Like, sometimes I’ll be at the bank, just counting money, and I’ll hear my name whispered, or see a customer look at me a certain way, and I just *know* they’re talking about me, or that there’s some hidden message in what they’re doing. It doesn’t happen all the time, but enough to make me feel really uneasy and always on edge.

And my body just feels weird sometimes. I’ll be standing, doing dishes or something, and I just… freeze. My arm will stay up in the air for ages, or I’ll just hold a pose, and it’s like I can’t move until it feels right. My husband, bless his heart, he just says I’m tired, but it's more than that. I just can’t seem to snap out of it. It’s hard to explain, but it’s making everything so much harder. I even feel like I'm not myself, like something happened, but I can't quite put my finger on it. It’s all just very confusing.
D005-D018_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D005-D018_h011.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h012.question: It’s like my brain just… changed. For about four months now, I've had this constant nagging feeling that my girlfriend, Sarah, is cheating on me. I see her talking to guys online, even just friendly comments, and my mind just goes to the worst possible place. I find myself checking her phone, looking at her social media a dozen times a day, even though she hasn't given me any real reason to doubt her. It’s exhausting. And everything just feels… off. I’ll be editing a video, and suddenly I’ll hear what sounds like someone repeating a line from the audio I’m working on, even if it's muted. It's subtle, but it's there. Sometimes if someone says something to me, I'll catch myself repeating the last few words they said under my breath without even meaning to. I'm not really sure why; it just happens. Things have just been really different since that incident a while back, but I don't really want to get into that right now. It just feels like I'm not in control, and it's making it hard to focus on my freelance work.

A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia

    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D005-D018_h013.question: "Lately, I just haven't been myself, not for about four months now. It's like my mind plays tricks on me. D005-D018_h014.question: "It's been... I don't know, about four months now, since things started feeling really off. I keep seeing things, usually when I'm alone in the house, cleaning. D005-D018_h015.question: I've been feeling… off, these past four months. Ever since my husband passed, things have just been strange. D005-D018_h016.question:
It's been about three months now, and honestly, it’s getting harder to just… function. I used to love my job, the energy of live television, but lately, it feels like my tongue is thick, and the words just won’t come out. When they do, sometimes they just… *rhyme*, you know? And then there are these feelings, these crawling sensations. I’ve been convinced there’s something wrong with my organs, like my liver just isn’t… right. No doctor has found anything, but I can feel it. It’s like bugs under my skin sometimes, especially when I’m alone. It's unsettling. I try to ignore it, to focus, but it’s constant. I just don't feel like myself anymore. It started after… well, after everything.

D005-D018_h017.question: It's been… maybe three months now? Everything just feels off. And getting up for my shifts, or just doing anything, really, it all feels so pointless. I used to love drawing, but now? I just… don’t. D005-D018_h018.question: It’s been about three months now, maybe a little more, since I started feeling really off. D005-D018_h019.question:
"It's been a rough few months, doctor. I'm 38, and a piano teacher, which I love, but lately, it's just...hard. I feel like my life is falling apart. My husband tries to understand, but I don't even understand it myself. It feels like someone is always watching me, judging every move. I'll be teaching a student, and out of the corner of my eye, I'll see someone standing there, a shadow figure, just lurking. Then I blink, and they're gone. It's disorienting.

It’s like my brain has a mind of its own. I find it so hard to get things done. Even simple tasks, like preparing my lessons, feel like climbing a mountain. I used to be so organized and motivated.

I had a really awful experience a while back, something I don't really want to get into. Maybe that's part of it? I don't know. It’s all just so confusing."

    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D005-D018_h020.question:
It’s been about three months now that things have felt… off. My wife, bless her heart, says I’m just stressed, but it’s more than that. I’ve started noticing patterns, almost like secret messages, in the weather reports – not just mine, but on the news too. Like the way the isobar lines cross, or a specific gust of wind… I know it sounds strange, but it feels like they’re trying to tell *me* something, specifically.

And then there are these tastes. Lately, everything has this faint, metallic tang, like old copper, that no one else seems to notice. It’s always there, no matter what I eat or drink, and sometimes it's so strong I can barely stomach my food. I try to explain it away, but it's consistent.

My mind feels like a jumbled mess sometimes. I'll open my mouth to explain this complex frontal system, and the words just… scramble. It’s like a forecast ticker-tape gone haywire. People just stare at me, and I know I'm not making sense. Honestly, it’s why I've been less interested in going to work. The drive to even start my day, to get up and do anything purposeful, has just fizzled out. I just sort of exist.

I suppose it started after that hiking accident, when I fell and hit my head. They said I was fine, but… I don’t know. Maybe it’s just that. It's hard to tell what’s real anymore.
D005-D018_h020.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia
D005-D018_h020.answer: D & A. Schizophrenia & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D005-D018_h021.question:
